name: Huguenot Tunnel
scope: Operating N1 tunnel eastern (Worcester/northeastern) portal exterior, stone-clad asymmetric ventilation/wing structure, actual entrance opening and intrinsic attached approach bridge. The underground3.9kmbore, western portal, separate unfinished northern bore, mountain, public roads beyond the approach bridge, toll plaza, vehicles and traffic equipment are excluded.
era: Surviving operating eastern portal, photo-guided from the exact cleared2012Qualla CC0original; concealed elevations/sections approximate.

review.method: Exact full-size cleared published QuallaCC0original inspected; native operating bore/approach bridge identity inspected separately.
review.notes: Exact3648x2736ZaianCC0Qualla-published original inspected. It shows an asymmetric small-rectangular multicolor stone facade, wide dark rectangular road opening with pale oxidized metal fascia, tall stepped masonry ventilation mass left of narrow pale green vertical fins, sloping wing roofs, small closed service doors and attached concrete road bridge with slit parapets and angled supports. Caption says northern entrance, referring to the northeastern end; native operating N1tunnelway/attachedbridge distinguish this portal from the separate unfinished NorthBore. Hidden rear, scale and engineering sections remain medium-fi estimates. No mountain/trees/vehicles copied.
